rule_for_the_interval: Claude does NOT steer ordinary HCLI engineering: no substrate repair, no prompt edits, no state edits, no phase corrections, no choosing or hinting at a defect. Claude continues Odyssey science on CPU, which is a different front and does not touch the body. Reading the campaign log and evidence is observation, not intervention.
what_breaks_the_interval_legitimately: the resident dies or wedges (a mechanic call, recorded as such and the interval restarted)
a NEW supervisor false positive is found (the measurement instrument is wrong, and a wrong instrument makes the whole interval void)
what_does_NOT_break_it: the body failing a phase repeatedly -- that is the measurement
the body picking a defect Claude thinks is uninteresting

interval_events.significance: the FIRST cycle to run entirely on the new substrate. Not acted on: one timeout is a data point, two consecutive is a pattern, and raising REQ_TIMEOUT on one sample would be fixing a guess.
interval_events.resident_state_when_checked: 1.2-1.7% CPU, idle -- so not still generating
interval_events.cause: NOT the new substrate. Checked the full soft-terminal history rather than reasoning from one sample: TimeoutError at REQ_TIMEOUT is CHRONIC and long predates today's changes -- cycle 9 timed out three times consecutively (23:25, 23:34, 23:42), cycle 34 twice (05:03, 05:24), and both recovered and the campaign continued past cycle 65. A single timeout at cycle 77 sits inside the established pattern and is not evidence about the new substrate at all.
interval_events.why_this_matters_for_the_interval: The working hypothesis was that the fixes made cycles too slow -- tests.run can now run a 154s suite and the prompt budget rose 45%, so a cycle needing >1200s was plausible. The history refutes it. Had REQ_TIMEOUT been raised on that reasoning it would have been a change made against a real pattern that the change had nothing to do with.

interval_events.event: an Odyssey job allocated 38.7 GiB alongside the resident
interval_events.defect: organ_gate_transfer allocated a d x d float64 Hessian PER ORGAN per layer. gate and up read the same activations and need the same H; keying by (layer, input_dim) makes sharing structural.
interval_events.was_it_the_cause_of_the_timeout: NO, and the first answer was wrong. The initial reading said free memory had fallen to 16.9 GiB, which looked like a resource collision with the resident. It was a measurement bug: the guard multiplied page counts by 4096 on a machine whose page size is 16384, a 4x undercount. Actual availability was ~68-72 GiB throughout. The collision hypothesis is withdrawn.
interval_events.the_worse_bug_that_bug_would_have_caused: the same undercount would have made the resource guard refuse EVERY future job while claiming to protect the resident -- a ceiling compared against a number that can never reach it, which is a latch. Same shape as the swap high-water defect that once held the resident at cycles=0 with 42.6 GB free. The page size is now read from vm_stat's own header rather than assumed.
interval_events.kept_fix: the per-organ Hessian was still a real bug and is fixed regardless

hypotheses_withdrawn_in_this_interval: the Odyssey job's 38.7 GiB starved the resident -- withdrawn, the memory reading was a 4x page-size undercount
the new substrate made cycles exceed 1200s -- withdrawn, timeouts are chronic across cycles 9, 34 and 77

outcome.which_close_condition: INFORMATIVE_FAILURE: 'the body is refused for a NEW reason, naming a defect nobody had found'. It did, and the defect had been live for the whole of experiment 2.
outcome.the_finding: H-MANIFESTO.md is 45,226 bytes, has NEVER been committed, and is therefore absent from the worktree where HCLI works. The harness objective names it TWICE -- as the thing HCLI develops toward, and as the worked example of a path to fs.read. Cycle 77's trace: the body's first call is fs.read H-MANIFESTO.md -> FileNotFoundError, then two real file reads, then FOUR web.search calls for 'H-MANIFESTO', '"H-MANIFESTO"' and 'H-MANIFESTO file' -- searching the public internet for a private uncommitted document.
outcome.what_the_body_said_about_it: 'HYPOTHESIS: I cannot name one yet -- I am still orienting; the first reads returned only 4 KB of 308 KB'. It was telling the truth twice over: it cannot orient toward a manifesto it has never been able to open, and tool results are truncated at RESULT_CHARS=3000.
outcome.why_it_took_this_long_to_see: the reply text alone never showed it. It was visible only in the TOOL TRACE, which cycles only began persisting this morning -- added after a supervisor false positive proved reply text insufficient to tell what a cycle had done. The instrument built to close one defect immediately exposed a larger one.
outcome.answer_to_the_interval_question: The interval asked whether what remains is substrate or the body. The answer for this cycle is SUBSTRATE, and not marginally: the body was told to orient on an unreadable file and reported that accurately. That is now seven substrate defects in a row that the body identified correctly and was blamed for.
